_note: REQ-TPR-1 and MAS-CSO-TPR records for the external services the inventory declares (scripts/build-ksi-signal.py build_external_components). Each names the upstream offering, the upstream component's identifier, the split between what the upstream runs and what this provider configures, and the four things FedRAMP requires documented for each third-party information resource (MAS-CSO-TPR): general usage and configuration, justification for use, mitigation measures, and compensating controls. A record is published only once it carries decided_by and decided_on, and a decided record must carry all four MAS-CSO-TPR fields or the build fails; until a decision, the inventory publishes every field as "not recorded". A record for a service the inventory does not declare fails the build. AI-drafted entries (drafted_by) were proposed from the evidence listed; the decision fields on the 2026-11-05 drafts are for the operator to confirm. A null value is unknown and is published as "not recorded" even after a decision.

ext::sigstore-fulcio.upstream_offering: Sigstore public-good instance: Fulcio certificate authority

responsibility_split.upstream_runs: The certificate authority that issues short-lived signing certificates bound to the CI run's OIDC identity.
responsibility_split.provider_configures: Keyless signing in CI (cosign sign-blob), and the certificate identity and OIDC issuer every verification pins.

ext::sigstore-fulcio.usage_and_configuration: Every deploy and nightly signs each published artifact keylessly: cosign obtains a short-lived certificate from Fulcio bound to the workflow's GitHub OIDC identity. No account or configuration exists on Fulcio's side.
ext::sigstore-fulcio.justification: Keyless signing removes long-lived signing keys from the pipeline and binds every signature to the exact workflow and commit that produced it, which any reader can verify.
ext::sigstore-fulcio.mitigations: Every verification pins the certificate identity (the workflow path and ref) and the OIDC issuer, so a certificate issued to anyone else does not verify. Fulcio sees only the CSR and the OIDC token claims (repository, workflow, ref), never artifact content. No federal customer data is in this offering; the resource never receives app-user data.
ext::sigstore-fulcio.compensating_controls: The post-publish round-trip verify and scripts/verify-published.sh re-verify every signature from outside; a Fulcio outage stops the deploy (fail closed) rather than publishing unsigned evidence.
ext::sigstore-fulcio.drafted_by: Claude (AI-drafted), 2026-11-03; MAS-CSO-TPR fields and decision fields AI-drafted 2026-11-05 for the operator to confirm

ext::sigstore-rekor.upstream_offering: Sigstore public-good instance: Rekor transparency log

responsibility_split.upstream_runs: The append-only transparency log and its inclusion proofs.
responsibility_split.provider_configures: Signing with transparency-log upload (cosign defaults, not disabled) and verification that checks the inclusion proof in each bundle.

ext::sigstore-rekor.usage_and_configuration: Each keyless signature is recorded in Rekor (cosign default, not disabled); the bundle published next to each artifact carries the inclusion proof.
ext::sigstore-rekor.justification: The transparency log makes every signature publicly auditable, so a signature made outside the pipeline would be visible.
ext::sigstore-rekor.mitigations: Rekor receives only the signature, certificate and artifact digest, never artifact content. Verification checks the inclusion proof offline from the bundle. No federal customer data is in this offering; the resource never receives app-user data.
ext::sigstore-rekor.compensating_controls: Signature verification against the pinned identity does not depend on Rekor being reachable later; the published bundles carry the proofs.
ext::sigstore-rekor.drafted_by: Claude (AI-drafted), 2026-11-03; MAS-CSO-TPR fields and decision fields AI-drafted 2026-11-05 for the operator to confirm

responsibility_split.upstream_runs: The token issuer and its signing keys (JWKS).
responsibility_split.provider_configures: Which workflows may request a token (permissions: id-token: write), the AWS IAM OIDC trust conditions, and the issuer pinned in cosign verification.

ext::github-oidc.usage_and_configuration: Workflows granted id-token: write obtain per-run identity tokens, which AWS STS exchanges for the deploy, plan and nightly roles and which Fulcio binds into signing certificates.
ext::github-oidc.justification: Workload identity replaces static cloud credentials in CI: there is no long-lived access key to leak.
ext::github-oidc.mitigations: The AWS role trust policies pin the repository and, for the deploy role, the prod environment (reviewer-gated); only named workflows request tokens. No federal customer data is in this offering; the resource never receives app-user data.
ext::github-oidc.compensating_controls: The deploy needs a human approval in the prod environment before its token can assume the deploy role; role permissions are least-privilege and reviewed in the bootstrap stack.
ext::github-oidc.drafted_by: Claude (AI-drafted), 2026-11-03; MAS-CSO-TPR fields and decision fields AI-drafted 2026-11-05 for the operator to confirm

responsibility_split.upstream_runs: Repository hosting, the Actions runners, Dependabot, and secret scanning.
responsibility_split.provider_configures: Branch protection on main, the workflows and their permissions, the OPA gate, the SCN tag validator, and secret scanning with push protection.

ext::github-repo.usage_and_configuration: Hosts the source of record and runs the CI/CD workflows (deploy, nightly evidence, scans) on GitHub-hosted runners.
ext::github-repo.justification: The repository is the system of record for infrastructure as code and evidence generation; hosted runners give an ephemeral, reproducible build environment.
ext::github-repo.mitigations: Branch protection on main, required checks, a reviewer-gated prod environment for every deploy, secret scanning with push protection, and least-privilege workflow permissions. No federal customer data is in this offering; the resource never receives app-user data.
ext::github-repo.compensating_controls: Every published artifact is signed under the deploy workflow's pinned identity and re-verified from outside; the hand-applied GitHub settings are checked live on every deploy (scripts/check-manual-settings.py).
ext::github-repo.drafted_by: Claude (AI-drafted), 2026-11-03; MAS-CSO-TPR fields and decision fields AI-drafted 2026-11-05 for the operator to confirm

responsibility_split.upstream_runs: The authenticator app that generates the time-based one-time codes.
responsibility_split.provider_configures: Enrollment of the TOTP device as the MFA factor on the AWS root account, the operator IAM user and the GitHub account.

ext::duo-mfa.usage_and_configuration: Generates the TOTP codes the operator enters as the second factor for the AWS root account, the operator IAM user and the GitHub account. AWS records both principals' MFA as virtual (TOTP) devices (DEC-025, DEC-150), which the deploy checks on every run; Duo does not enforce anything.
ext::duo-mfa.justification: A second factor on every top-level administrative and privileged account, as IA-2(1) and IA-2(2) require.
ext::duo-mfa.mitigations: TOTP seeds stay on the operator's device; no tenant identifier is published. MFA is enabled on every privileged human account. No federal customer data is in this offering; the resource never receives app-user data.
ext::duo-mfa.compensating_controls: The weaker-than-phishing-resistant factor is a recorded decision (DEC-025); CloudTrail records every console sign-in and privileged API call.
evidence: scripts/build-ksi-signal.py (ext::duo-mfa: tenant identifier intentionally not published)
ext::duo-mfa.drafted_by: Claude (AI-drafted), 2026-11-05; decided by the operator 2026-11-05. The repository records virtual TOTP MFA on the root user and the operator user (DEC-025, DEC-150); that Duo Mobile is the app generating the codes is the operator's statement (docs/rules-of-behavior.md, docs/policies/ia-policy.md).

ext::anchore-grype-db.upstream_offering: Grype vulnerability database, distributed by Anchore

responsibility_split.upstream_runs: Building and publishing the vulnerability database from upstream advisory sources.
responsibility_split.provider_configures: The pinned Grype version (GRYPE_VERSION) and the scans of each SBOM in the deploy and the nightly.

ext::anchore-grype-db.usage_and_configuration: Grype downloads the current database at scan time and matches every SBOM the pipeline builds against it.
ext::anchore-grype-db.justification: The primary software-composition scan behind the VDR.
ext::anchore-grype-db.mitigations: The Grype version is pinned; Grype checks the database download against the checksum in its published index. Only the SBOMs are scanned, locally; nothing is uploaded. No federal customer data is in this offering; the resource never receives app-user data.
ext::anchore-grype-db.compensating_controls: Dependabot alerts and CISA KEV are independent sources the VDR corroborates against.
ext::anchore-grype-db.drafted_by: Claude (AI-drafted), 2026-11-05, for the operator to confirm

responsibility_split.upstream_runs: Serving the published npm package files over its CDN.
responsibility_split.provider_configures: The pinned MediaPipe Tasks Vision version in the app bundle and the CSP script-src and connect-src paths that allow only that package.

ext::jsdelivr.usage_and_configuration: The Silk Reeling app's browser code loads the MediaPipe Tasks Vision JavaScript and WebAssembly from jsDelivr at the version the bundle pins.
ext::jsdelivr.justification: MediaPipe runs pose estimation in the user's browser, so camera frames never leave the device; jsDelivr is the distribution MediaPipe documents.
ext::jsdelivr.mitigations: The CSP allows only the pinned package path; camera frames stay in the browser and only pose landmarks reach the app's API. jsDelivr sees the user's IP address and user agent when the file is fetched. No federal customer data is in this offering; the resource never receives app-user data.
ext::jsdelivr.compensating_controls: The app requires Cognito sign-in with TOTP MFA; the API accepts only landmark data and returns scores. Self-hosting the runtime is the further step if a stronger integrity guarantee is needed.
ext::jsdelivr.drafted_by: Claude (AI-drafted), 2026-11-05, for the operator to confirm

ext::google-cloud-storage.upstream_offering: Google Cloud Storage, MediaPipe public model bucket

responsibility_split.upstream_runs: Hosting and serving the published MediaPipe model files.
responsibility_split.provider_configures: The model path the app requests and the CSP connect-src path that allows only the mediapipe-models bucket.

ext::google-cloud-storage.usage_and_configuration: The MediaPipe runtime in the user's browser downloads the pose-landmarker model file from Google's public model bucket.
ext::google-cloud-storage.justification: The model Google publishes for MediaPipe pose landmarking; running it in the browser keeps camera frames on the device.
ext::google-cloud-storage.mitigations: The CSP allows only the mediapipe-models path; the model is data loaded by the pinned runtime, not script. Google sees the user's IP address and user agent when the file is fetched. No federal customer data is in this offering; the resource never receives app-user data.
ext::google-cloud-storage.compensating_controls: Pose scores are computed server-side from landmarks only; a tampered model could degrade scores but cannot read data beyond the camera frames already in the browser.
ext::google-cloud-storage.drafted_by: Claude (AI-drafted), 2026-11-05, for the operator to confirm
